Ji Sung Park (박지성) is a former professional footballer from South Korea, widely regarded as one of the most accomplished Asian players in European football history. He was born on January 25, 1981, in Seoul, South Korea. Park played primarily as a midfielder and was known for his versatility, work rate, passing ability, and tactical intelligence.

**Career Highlights**

| Club | Years | Appearances | Goals |
|------|-------|-------------|-------|
| **Ulsan Hyundai** | 1999–2000 | 30 | 5 |
| **VfB Stuttgart** | 2000–2004 | 112 | 12 |
| **Arsenal** | 2004–2011 | 210 | 15 |
| **Manchester City** | 2011–2012 | 20 | 0 |
| **VfL Wolfsburg** | 2012–2013 | 27 | 1 |
| **FC Augsburg** | 2013–2014 | 23 | 0 |
| **FC Seoul** | 2014–2015 | 28 | 1 |

- **International Career** – Park earned 108 caps for the South Korean national team, scoring 13 goals. He represented South Korea at three FIFA World Cups (2002, 2006, 2010) and was part of the squad that finished third in the 2002 World Cup, earning him the Bronze Ball award.
- **Awards & Honors** – He was named the Asian Footballer of the Year in 2004 and 2008, and he won the Premier League title with Arsenal in 2005–06. In 2007, he was selected for the UEFA Team of the Year.
- **Post‑Playing Career** – After retiring from professional football, Park has worked as a football analyst and commentator for various sports networks in South Korea. He also serves as a goodwill ambassador for the Korean Football Association and has been involved in youth development programs.

**Legacy**

Park is celebrated for breaking barriers for Asian players in Europe, setting a precedent for future generations such as Shinji Kagawa, Hwang Hee-chan, and Son Heung‑min. His professionalism, humility, and dedication to the sport have made him a role model both on and off the pitch.
